title: weed/s3api and the filer — code graph
subtitle: File-level map of SeaweedFS's S3 gateway, its satellite catalog APIs and the filer underneath: 101 files of package s3api, 40 files of the Iceberg REST catalog, Lance namespace and S3 Vectors servers, 83 filer, filer_pb and filer gRPC server files plus the generated filer protocol, and 13 collapsed packages; lanes run from the S3 request down to the filer.
intro: weed/s3api is SeaweedFS's S3-compatible gateway. It is a gorilla/mux HTTP server that authenticates each request (SigV4/V2, presigned URLs, STS/JWT, embedded IAM and bucket policies) and maps the S3 operation onto the filer tree under BucketsPath. On top of filer entries and volume chunks it implements the features S3 clients expect: multipart uploads, versioning, SSE-C/KMS/S3, object lock, tagging, ACLs, CORS and lifecycle. Edges come only from the AST (graphify): symbol-level calls, type references, function values passed (indirect_call, e.g. route registration), embeds and imports, aggregated to file level. Lanes 8-10 add the three catalog servers that run beside the gateway on their own ports (wired in command/s3.go): the Iceberg REST catalog, the Lance Namespace REST server and the AWS-compatible S3 Vectors API. All three keep their records in the S3 Tables catalog (the s3tables/ node); lane 11 is the plugin worker that maintains Iceberg tables by writing the filer directly. Lanes 12-19 are the filer the gateway runs on: the filer.proto contract and filer_pb client helpers, the filer gRPC handlers the gateway calls (conditional writes, object transactions routed to a key's owner filer, metadata subscriptions), namespace operations, entries and stores, chunks and the read path, the metadata log and peer aggregation, remote mounts, and background deletion and empty-folder cleanup. The gateway reaches lane 13 only over gRPC, so the filer.proto node is where the two halves meet. No dependency rule is enforced. Those servers register their routes with unexported method values, which the extractor does not draw, so their handler files show no incoming edge from server.go.

scope.seeds: weed/s3api/*.go, weed/s3api/{iceberg,lance,s3vectors}/*.go, weed/filer/*.go, weed/filer/empty_folder_cleanup/*.go, weed/pb/filer_pb/*.go (hand-written) and weed/server/filer_grpc_server*.go (non-test)
scope.neighbors: weed/s3api/{s3err,s3_constants,policy_engine,s3tables,s3lifecycle,s3lifecycle/scheduler,lifecycle_xml,s3bucket,cors,s3_objectlock,policy}/ weed/worker/tasks/iceberg/ and weed/filer/abstract_sql/ collapsed to one node each; the generated filer_pb code is one node, weed/pb/filer.proto
scope.excluded: *_test.go, s3tables/s3tablestest, s3lifecycle/lifecycletest, iceberg/testdata, worker/tasks/iceberg/testdata, policy_engine/examples.go (go:build ignore), kms_azure.go (azurekms build tag), weed/filer/filer_notify_read_testing.go and meta_aggregator_testing.go (test hooks); the individual filer store backends; import fan-out edges into file nodes
scope.why_criterion: consequence if it fails + design decision + AWS compatibility constraint
